description.value: A historic mountain lodge-resort above Naramata Bench where the Kettle Valley Railway trail passes the front door, offering private wooded campsites with access to lodge washrooms, showers, and a full restaurant; the 11 km gravel approach road is maintained but unpaved and the KVR itself is dirt with bumps and potholes.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website (chutelakelodge.ca) provides rich detail across multiple subpages. Key evidence: the FAQ confirms bike racks on site, WiFi in the lodge, showers accessible to campers via the lodge building, a full-service on-site restaurant, and e-bike rentals; the About page explicitly states the KVR railway in front of the lodge 'was converted into one of the best cycling paths in the province.' OSM records the name as 'Chute Lake Resort' but the website consistently and unambiguously uses 'Chute Lake Lodge'; the website value is used per Rule 12 and the discrepancy is flagged in concerns. OSM contained no phone or address to cross-check, so those contact_confirmed fields are null.
concerns: Name mismatch: OSM records 'Chute Lake Resort' but the website consistently uses 'Chute Lake Lodge'; listing name updated to website value.
Contact email domain (book@chutelakelodgeresort.ca) differs from website domain (chutelakelodge.ca) — likely a legacy domain, but worth noting.
OSM tags are sparse (only name and tourism=camp_site); no phone or address in OSM to cross-check against website values.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Chute Lake Lodge sits directly on the Kettle Valley Railway cycling trail and offers campsites, lodge-accessible showers, an on-site restaurant, bike racks, and e-bike rentals — a strong and well-evidenced fit for the WWC cycling tourism directory.
enrichment_extras.notes: E-bike rentals available on site per FAQ ('rentals on E-Bikes, canoes, paddle boards, fishing gear'). Bike racks provided but lodge explicitly states it is 'not liable or responsible in any way for bikes and bike storage' — no secured storage. Final 11 km of access road is maintained gravel; website advises approaching from Penticton (south) rather than Kelowna (north).

wow_evidence: bike racks on site… e-bike rentals; KVR trail passes the front door, 'converted into one of the best cycling paths in the province'
